title: With Vendor Order Management View only, starting a return is as today
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have a ShopView account on production (app.shopview.com, which does not have this release yet) where you can create a role and a staff member, so today's access can be seen beside the build's.
  • Create the same custom role for this test on the build and on production, role B, with Vendor Order Management — View, without Vendor Order Management — Create & Edit, and with Part Library & Inventory — View, so the two can be compared.
  • Create a staff member, user B, with role B on the build and on production, so the steps run with role B's permissions on both.
  • Use window 1 signed in as user B on the build and window 2 signed in as user B on production.
custom_steps:
1. In window 1, click Parts in the top bar.
  2. In window 1, click Returns in the left menu.
  3. In window 2, click Parts in the top bar.
  4. In window 2, click Returns in the left menu.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Parts left menu opens on the build for user B.

Step 2:

  • The Returns list opens on the build; note whether the button that starts a new return is shown and usable, shown greyed out, or missing.

Step 3:

  • Production's Parts left menu opens for user B.

Step 4:

  • Production's Returns list opens, and its button that starts a new return is in the same state as on the build.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10822 (Story 9, Inactive Parts Cannot Be Added to New Work), story SV-10825 (Story 12, Call the Shared Parts List the Part Library)

  • S9-N3a: “Opening Parts → Returns and starting a vendor return keep the access today's 'Vendor Order Management' settings give. This feature adds, removes and changes no permission (S12-N1). 'Vendor Order Management → Create & Edit' includes 'Part Library & Inventory → View', so a role with it can search for parts on a return.”
  • S12-N1: “No permission is added, removed or re-keyed. Every user's access on release day is identical to the day before.”
  • Key Decisions: “Access does not change. Retiring a part, bringing it back and changing its tracking use the same access ShopView applies to deleting an inventory part today. The controls show to exactly the users who see Delete on the part dialog today. The system accepts exactly the users it accepts a delete from today, on every route. No user gains or loses access on release day (Story 8).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
